title: Book One · Chapter 20: A Good Afternoon
story:
Dad plans to wash the room floor on Tuesday afternoon. Mum plans to finish two small repairs. Ronan has questions about the kite string. He wants to ask Dad this afternoon.

Then Mrs Lan comes out. The family stops work to listen.

Mrs Lan comes into the yard with a bowl of small green beans.

"I bought too many," she says. "The man kept adding beans to my bag. Look how many there are!"

"Can you help me with these beans?" she asks Ronan. "Pull off these little ends." He sits beside her. Mum brings a second bowl. Dad moves the washing bucket out of the way.

At first Ronan snaps each bean exactly in half. Mrs Lan shows him the thin end.

"Only this bit. We want something left for dinner."

He learns to pull the little string along one side. He finds a string on some beans. On others, he cannot find one.

Dad tries. His first bean breaks in three places.

"Very good at small pieces," Mum says.

Dad puts all three pieces in the bowl. "More beans for your money."

They work in the yard. A breeze moves the washing. The black cat lies under Mrs Lan's chair. Ronan drops a bean end. The cat looks at it and closes its eyes again.

"It doesn't eat greens," Mrs Lan says.

"How does it know they're green with its eyes shut?" Ronan asks.

Mum laughs. A bean falls under the board. Dad gets it before the cat does.

After the beans are done, Mum brings out the two pears from the fruit shop. She cuts each into pieces. One side is brown and soft. She cuts that away.

Ronan picks the piece with the longest stem. He takes a bite. It tastes sweeter than he expects.

Mrs Lan has work to do in the front room. She takes her bowls away. She leaves some beans for their dinner. Dad says the floor can wait until the yard is clear.

"What about a walk first?" Mum asks.

They go to the river path, away from the road. There is a low wall between the path and the water. Ronan stays beside Mum. Ronan watches light on the water. The water moves. The light moves too.

Dad finds two dry leaves. Ronan finds a third, smaller leaf. They put the leaves on the wall. The wind blows toward the dry grass. It takes the leaves away from the river.

They race the leaves along the path. Mum's leaf catches in a crack. Dad's turns over. Part of Ronan's leaf is missing. His little leaf goes farthest.

"I win," Ronan says.

"Your leaf wins," Mum says. "You were very slow."

He runs three steps ahead and waits with his hands on his hips. Dad walks slower on purpose.

At home, they wash the floor together. Ronan does the space by the door with his own cloth. Mum finishes the sewing after dinner. Dad holds the lamp closer. Ronan reads two pages of his boat book. Mum helps with a few words.

The kite stays on its board. No money goes into the tea box.

Before bed, Ronan draws three leaves on a scrap of paper. He puts the smallest one far ahead of the others. He shows Mum and Dad the small leaf at the front. They smile. They remember the race too.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：sweeter＝更甜；beans＝豆角；leaf＝叶子；path＝小路。

理解问题：

1. 一家人为什么临时改变下午的安排？
2. 这个下午有哪些不需要很多钱的快乐？
